method.mechanism: Agent hypothesis: compression-induced changes in representation direction can retain ranking benefits when representation norms are restored. Let h be the incumbent final representation and z=4*tanh(h/4). The candidate returns z*sqrt(max(sum(h^2),1e-12)/max(sum(z^2),1e-12)); the generated control returns z. Outside the denominator-floor regime, candidate and control have identical directions but different norms on identical upstream states. Consequently, their fixed-state candidate rankings agree in exact arithmetic; any trained ranking difference requires training adaptation or numerical effects. Norm restoration does not guarantee numerical robustness or resolve the historical provenance discrepancy.

method.mechanism: Agent hypothesis: float64 accumulation of masked normalized states may reduce rounding error in strictly preceding context means and associated cutoff-rank sensitivity. Candidate promotes masked states before cumulative summation, divides in float64, then casts context back to x.dtype. The generated control accumulates in the incumbent dtype but performs the same float64 division and final cast. This isolates accumulation precision from division precision without changing the mathematical aggregation, blend coefficients or parameterization. It cannot resolve checkpoint provenance, guarantee reproducibility or establish that numerical error caused the reported discrepancy.
